entries.why: the prompt of the box for an ntfy access token, which only a server with access control needs — access token as your 1.x word for it — 1.12 C7, C13

entries.key: Set host, user, from and to in tokenPace.notifications.email first.
entries.why: a setup check with the button Open Settings: host, user, from and to are the names of the setting’s fields and stay in English, as tokenPace.notifications.email does — 1.12 C13

entries.key: The password or app password of {0} on the SMTP server. It is kept in VS Code's secret storage.
entries.why: the prompt of the box for the mail password — {0} is the SMTP user name as the reader set it (often an address such as name@example.com), an app password is one a mail provider makes for one program (German: App-Passwort), SMTP stays — secret storage is VS Code’s SecretStorage — a description, not a product name (German: der geschützte Speicher von VS Code) — use one phrase for it in every key of this setup — 1.12 C7, C13

entries.key: Allow Token Pace to send notifications to {0}?
entries.why: the consent’s title, a modal question asked after the address and secrets were typed and before anything is stored — {0} is the host the messages go to (hooks.slack.com, api.telegram.org, ntfy.sh or smtp.example.com:587) — your word for notification from the category Notifications (n=40) — 1.12 C6, C13

entries.key: Token Pace will send a short message to {0} over an encrypted connection when one of the events you list in tokenPace.notifications.events happens — at most once per event and quota window, and at most one message of a kind every tokenPace.notifications.cooldownMinutes minutes.
entries.why: the consent’s first paragraph — {0} is the host as in n=97 — keep tokenPace.notifications.events and tokenPace.notifications.cooldownMinutes as they stand, an encrypted connection is TLS, quota window as your 1.x word for it — 1.12 C6, C13

entries.key: A message holds only the event, the program or provider, the quota window, percentages and times — never a prompt, a line of a transcript, a path, a project, a session's name or id, or anything Claude Code or Codex wrote.
entries.why: the consent’s second paragraph: what a notification holds and never holds — keep Claude Code and Codex, prompt and session as your 1.x words for them — 1.12 C6, C13

entries.key: The address and its secret stay in VS Code's secret storage on this machine, never in settings.json. Token Pace reads nothing back from {0} except whether it accepted the message.
entries.why: the consent’s third paragraph — {0} is the host as in n=97 — secret storage is VS Code’s SecretStorage — a description, not a product name (German: der geschützte Speicher von VS Code) — use one phrase for it in every key of this setup — keep settings.json as it stands — 1.12 C6, C13

entries.key: You can take this back with "Token Pace: Remove a Notification Channel…".
entries.why: the consent’s fourth paragraph: it quotes the command’s title as your translation of command.notifications.remove.title (n=80) writes it, with Token Pace: before it, inside your quotation marks — 1.12 C6, C13

entries.key: Notifications: {0} is set up. To use it, add "{1}" to tokenPace.notifications.channels.
entries.why: the answer after Set Up — {0} is the channel’s name as Set Up’s list shows it (Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Mattermost, Rocket.Chat, Telegram, ntfy, or your Webhook (JSON) and E-mail (SMTP)) — the pronouns after it follow your word for channel, not the service’s name (German: Kanal, ihn, seine) — {1} is the channel’s id in the setting (webhook, telegram, ntfy or email), English, inside your quotation marks — keep tokenPace.notifications.channels as it stands, Notifications: as your category’s word — 1.12 C8, C13

entries.key: Notifications: {0} is set up. To use it, add "{1}" to tokenPace.notifications.channels and set the format in tokenPace.notifications.webhook to "{2}".
entries.why: the same answer for a webhook whose format setting differs from the one just set up — {0} is the channel’s name as Set Up’s list shows it (Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Mattermost, Rocket.Chat, Telegram, ntfy, or your Webhook (JSON) and E-mail (SMTP)) — the pronouns after it follow your word for channel, not the service’s name (German: Kanal, ihn, seine) — {1} as in n=102, {2} the webhook’s format (slack, discord, teams, mattermost, rocketChat or generic), English, inside your quotation marks — keep both settings’ names as they stand — 1.12 C8, C13

entries.key: No notification channel is set up yet. Run "Token Pace: Set Up a Notification Channel…" first.

the button of that question (n=109): the channel is removed when it is clicked — a verb as your other dialog buttons write one (German: Entfernen) — 1.12 C13

entries.key: Notifications: {0} was removed — its secrets and its consent are gone.

entries.key: `tokenPace.quotaSource` is `cache`: only a local file is read for the quota; the network is never used for it.
entries.why: the explanation of the status bar’s quota off in the cache mode, now scoped to the quota: for the quota only a local file is read and the network is never used for it (was: only a local file is read, the network is never used) — since 1.12 a notification channel the reader set up may still send, so the sentence no longer says that the network is never used at all — keep `tokenPace.quotaSource` and `cache` as they stand, quota as your 1.x word for it — 1.12 Review 3 F6
